args.text:
If you’re a program manager or a federal web developer, chances are you’ve been handed what looks like a simple job: build a website as part of an initiative at your agency. The hardest part often isn’t writing the content or designing the site, it’s getting the security and privacy compliance sorted so you can launch the actual website and keep it running. For that work, you might have to bring in a contractor or pile extra load on your agency’s web team.

It shouldn’t be that way.

## Why Pages?

Pages looks after our fellow federal partners by expertly handling the backend and compliance work it takes to launch and run a website, so you can put your know-how into your content.

- **FedRAMP Certified Platform** Pages is hosted on cloud.gov, a platform with security and compliance verified by the FedRAMP Joint Authorization Board, which means you can count on your site being fast, reliable, and ready for unexpected spikes in traffic.

- **Easy previews and content approvals** Pages builds draft updates to your site at a special preview URL. That way your team knows their changes will show up right when they’re pushed to the main site, and it’s easy to get the tick of approval on content updates from stakeholders.

[![Diagram of Pages architecture]({{site.baseurl}}/assets/images/pages/how-pages-works-diagram.png)]({{site.baseurl}}/assets/documents/how-pages-works-diagram.pdf)

## Why static websites?

Pages generates static websites instead of using a more complicated content management system (CMS) like Drupal or WordPress. Static websites have a few things going for them:

- **Less complexity and vulnerability:** Steering clear of a traditional CMS means steering clear of headaches like maintaining server applications (no PHP or Apache / IIS), on top of database scaling and redundancy. Production-level static sites generally need one simple static file server or service, not dozens. So the whole website is easier to maintain and has fewer vulnerabilities.

- **Update content without writing code:** Static websites often keep content in simple text files that anyone on the team can edit. The GitHub editor lets any team member make basic edits to their text files, whatever their experience writing code.

- **Easy to host and maintain:** It’s dead easy to host static website files on Pages. You can make the most of scaling services like Amazon S3 through Pages, where you only pay for what you use.

- **Fully customisable:** Designers and developers can shape static websites into whatever form they like without having to strip out CMS-provided features and defaults. Static sites can be used to build all sorts of sites, from organisation homepages or intranets to pre-generated web application program interfaces that display data from a separate server.

declined.reason: 'Pages builds out draft updates' is the software sense (generates a build); 'knock together' means put together roughly, which undercuts the claim
'build many different types of sites' is a product claim; 'knock together' says quick and rough
'properly easy' reads British; used 'dead easy' for 'very easy'
